title: Preferred home town
text: Home town used by travel and town activities for this character. Choices: Not set, Arthe Dale, Crossing, Knife Clan, Darkling Wood, Dirge, Fayrin's Rest, Chyolvea, Leth Deriel, Shard, Steelclaw Clan, Stone Clan, Tiger Clan, Wolf Clan, Riverhaven, Rossman's Landing, Therenborough, Langenfirth, Fornsted, Hvaral, Ratha, Aesry, Mer'Kresh, Throne City, Hibarnhvidar, Raven's Point, Boar Clan, Fang Cove,

title: Trash bin room
text: Room number of the room with the trash bin, for example 2026011. Scripts walk there to throw things away; the first use is memory orbs that could not be used. Leave at 0 for none. Set this together with the trash bin name. A number, at least 0, at most 999999999.

title: Trash bin name
text: What the trash bin in that room is called, as the game takes it in PUT MY ORB IN , for example bucket.

title: Subscription tier
text: Account type used by travel, banking, selling, and training. Choices: F2P, Standard, Premium.

title: Prime client controls at login
text: Run wrayth-prime automatically at login. It sends the Wrayth/StormFront client controls that unlock the game's larger typeahead queue, then exits. No gameplay commands are sent. Turn this off only to run a login without the larger queue. Yes or No.

title: Print experience gains
text: Print a line in the story window each time a skill's mind state goes up, such as First Aid(+2). Warnings about a skill that is learning poorly are printed whether this is on or off. Yes or No.

title: Typeahead
text: Number of movement commands allowed ahead of game output. Use 0 for careful movement.

title: Citizenship
text: Province citizenship used when choosing restricted travel crossings. Choices: Not set, Zoluren, Therengia, Ilithi, Qi'Reshalia, Forfedhdar.

title: Shard thief password
text: The password the Shard Thieves' Guild door asks for. Leave blank on characters who don't use that guild.

title: Connection: reconnect automatically
text: After an unexpected disconnect, log this character back in from the saved session, run reconnect-recovery, and restart master-train if it was running. A typed quit/exit, Disconnect, Exit, or closing GrayDR never reconnects. Yes or No.

title: Connection: reconnect grace (seconds)
text: Seconds to wait before the first reconnect attempt; the game refuses an immediate re-login while the character is still counted as logged in. Later attempts wait 2x, 3x, ... this long. A number, at least 0, at most 3600.

title: Connection: reconnect attempts
text: Maximum reconnect attempts per disconnect before giving up and leaving the window in its disconnected state. A number, at least 0, at most 100.

title: Connection: reconnects allowed per hour
text: How many times this character may be reconnected automatically within one hour. When the limit is reached it stays disconnected and says so. 0 = no limit. A number, at least 0, at most 100.

title: Chat: connect to LNet at startup
text: Connect this character to the LNet chat network (lnet.lichproject.org) when it logs in. Messages appear in the Thoughts window. Chat only: other players' requests for your location, skills or health are always answered with nothing. .chat connect / .chat disconnect switch it during a session. Yes or No.

title: Chat: LNet password
text: Optional. LNet names are first come, first served. Type .chat password once to reserve this character's name, then put the same word here so every login uses it. Stored in plain text, as Lich does.

title: Safe room
text: Character-wide GrayDR room UID used whenever a script or Master Train entry refers to saferoom. A number, at least 0, at most 999999999. Must be a room on the map.

title: Trash container
text: Exact adjective and noun of the character's general trash container. Spellcasting uses it for spent runestones. Leave blank to use ordinary disposal behavior.

title: Trash container activation verb
text: Optional verb run after putting trash in the character's container, for example TURN. Leave blank when the container needs no activation.

title: Named rooms
text: Define reusable names for GrayDR room UIDs. Enter a name such as enchantingroom here once, then use that name in any Master Train Room field. Built-in names such as saferoom, magicroom, engineeringroom, outfittingroom, and pickingroom resolve from their existing settings without being repeated here. A table of name and value pairs (value: GrayDR room UID).

title: Script prefix
text: Typing this prefix before a name runs that script (for example .master-train). Leave empty to disable.

title: Bare commands
text: Space-separated script names that run without the prefix, like game commands (default: go2). Pick names the game will never use; remove a name here if the game ever claims it.

title: Bare-word aliases
text: Semicolon-separated name=expansion pairs. Typing the bare name runs the full expansion (for example spot=go2 2030; home=go2 10028).

title: Vitality/spirit logout threshold
text: Under this vitality or spirit percent the AFK Monitor stops every other script and logs out. While a Hunt with its own Stop hunting below vitality is running, the Hunt leaves combat instead and the AFK Monitor stands down until the hunt is over. A number, at least 0, at most 100.

title: Depart automatically after death
text: Yes or No.

title: Justice complaints before logout
text: A number, at least 0.

title: Normal plain-text log
text: Record exactly the visible main-window text without timestamps or formatting. Yes or No.

title: Warning and error snapshots
text: Keep a 64 KB recent-text ring and write separate warning/error snapshots. The ring is released when this option is off. Yes or No.

title: Debug log
text: Full timestamped debug capture: everything shown in the window, every command sent with its owner, everything received, and command timing records. The standing diagnosis tool - leave it on. Authentication payloads are redacted. Yes or No.

title: Log directory
text: Leave blank for the shared profile logs directory, or choose another folder. Relative paths are resolved beside engine.yaml.

title: Memory heap watch
text: Write a per-minute memory ledger to the log directory: process totals, per-heap live vs committed bytes, window scrollback sizes, and queue depths. Costs one file line per minute; separates a real leak from allocator retention without a special measurement day. Yes or No.

title: Engine memory snapshots
text: Append the .memory engine report (per-script Lua heaps, journal, game-data cache) to the memory ledger automatically each minute - no typing .memory in every window. Yes or No.

title: Deep allocation tracing (heavy)
text: Record a call stack for every allocation in the process so a confirmed leak can be attributed to the exact code. WARNING: costs real CPU (~3x) - turn on only for a measurement session, then turn it off. Takes effect at the next GrayDR start; while on, the memory ledger includes the top unfreed call sites and scripts automatically get triple the engine time allowance so measurement overhead does no

title: Full pouches before handoff
text: On a giver, request a handoff after a completed hunt when this many full hunting or box-picking pouches are stored. Leave blank to disable giving. A number, at least 1.

title: Jewelry and keepsake boxes before handoff
text: On a giver, also request a handoff after a completed hunt when this many jewelry and keepsake boxes together (any mix) are in the full pouch container. Leave blank to count pouches only. A number, at least 1.

title: F2P: give excess platinum to the receiver
text: After the pouches, the giver hands Jang its platinum Dokoras above Platinum to keep, in one GIVE. Free-to-play allows one coin handoff per cooldown; when the game refuses with its handoff-limit line the platinum is kept and the handoff goes on. Dokoras only; gold, silver and copper stay. Yes or No.

title: F2P: platinum to keep
text: How many platinum Dokoras the giver keeps on hand; everything above it goes to Jang. A number, at least 0.

title: Handoff participants
text: Jang's fixed handoff order. Only Jang needs this list. A list.

title: Named gear sets
text: Map each set name (for example standard) to the full descriptions of items that should be worn. A table of name and value pairs.

title: Aim fillers
text: Actions sent in order while a bow or crossbow aims, one list per weapon skill, for example Bow: [perc, hide]. Used while Stealth is not being trained; the stealth list below is used otherwise. A table of name and value pairs.

title: Aim fillers stealth
text: The same as Aim fillers, used instead while Stealth still needs training. A table of name and value pairs.

title: Aiming trainables
text: Weapon skills to train with a weapon in the off hand while a crossbow aims. Each must also be in Weapon training. Keep them light. Add Tactics to train it the same way. A list.

title: Always use maneuvers
text: If true, keep using Charged Maneuvers regardless of field exp Yes or No.

title: Ambush
text: Yes: ambush from hiding instead of backstabbing (Thief). Yes or No.

title: Ambush location
text: The body part an ambush aims at, for example neck. Blank for no aim.

title: Ambush stun weapons
text: Weapon skills to train with Ambush Stun, separated by commas. While one of these is up the hunt hides and sends "ambush stun" instead of a normal attack. Needs Ambush Stun learned and a blunt weapon. Stops once Backstab is mind locked and starts again when it drops, unless Backstab past mindlock is on.

title: Ambush choke weapons
text: Weapon skills to train with Ambush Choke, separated by commas. While one of these is up the hunt hides and sends "ambush choke" instead of a normal attack. Any weapon works; needs Ambush Choke learned. Stops once Backstab is mind locked and starts again when it drops, unless Backstab past mindlock is on.

title: Armor exp training max threshold
text: Mind state at which the Armor skills listed under Stop on count as done. Every skillset has its own number.

title: Astrology prediction skills
text: Hash of skills to use for each prediction. A table of name and value pairs.

title: Attack overrides
text: The attack word to send instead of the usual one, per weapon skill, for example Small Edged: slice. A table of name and value pairs.

title: Aura frequency
text: Trader only - enables starlight management - how many seconds in between checking starlight auras in combat

title: Autoloot container
text: Name of autoloot container for Combat Trainer

title: Autoloot gems
text: Set to true if you have gems autolooted Yes or No.

title: Avtalia array
text: Trader-use avtalia.lic to build a list of avtalia cambrinth. A table of name and value pairs.

title: Backstab
text: The weapon skill from Weapon training used for backstabs. Several can be listed, one per row (Thief).

title: Backstab past mindlock
text: Useful for farming with backstab Yes or No.

title: Balance regen threshold
text: Minimum balance to perform certain actions (currently only whirlwind) solidly balanced

title: Barb famine healing
text: Barbarian Famine healing: healththreshold (use Famine below this health percent) and innerfirethreshold (only when inner fire is above this). Leave empty when unused. A table of name and value pairs.

title: Battle cries
text: Barbarian roars or Bard screams used in combat, taken in order. Each row names the cry and may add targetenemy, minthreshold and maxthreshold (how many creatures must be present) and a custom command. A list.

title: Battle cry cooldown
text: The number of seconds to wait between battle cries.

title: Battle cry cycle
text: The order to use the battle cries in, by name. Leave empty to take them in the order listed above. A list.

title: Bonebug
text: Necromancer: a row with make: Yes raises a bone bug from corpses in combat. Needs the bonebug spell set.

title: Box-hunt start threshold
text: Used only by Hunt entries configured as box-collection hunts. The Hunt runs when the character carries this many locked boxes or fewer; it is skipped when carrying more. This does not limit ordinary box looting.

title: Maximum boxes carried
text: Maximum total locked boxes to carry. Combat counts boxes already carried, loots until reaching this total, then leaves additional boxes. Leave blank to always loot boxes. A box-collection Hunt also ends when this total is reached. A number, at least 0.

title: Use charged maneuvers
text: No switches the whole charged-maneuver feature off for this character: the maneuver list below is ignored, "Charged Maneuver" in training abilities does nothing, and the Bow/dual-load conflict check is skipped. Yes (the default) keeps the Lich behavior. Native GrayDR switch; Lich has no equivalent. Yes or No.

title: Charged maneuvers
text: Charged maneuvers that train Expertise, per weapon skill, for example Small Edged: lunge. Needs Charged Maneuver in Training abilities with a cooldown. Dual Wield and Shield Usage rows give the dual-wield and shield-rush maneuvers. A table of name and value pairs.

title: Check discern timer in hours
text: With Use auto mana: hours between discerns of each spell. Lower circles should check more often.

title: Combat analyze retry count
text: How many times to retry a failed ANALYZE when Analyze is in Training abilities.

title: Combat spell timer
text: Seconds between casts of the Combat spell training spells. Too short starves other casting.

title: Combat spell training
text: Spells cast in combat to train each magic skill: one row per skill with the spell name, mana and the usual spell options, for example Warding: {name: Shield, mana: 10}. Cast on the timer above while mana is above the thresholds. A table of name and value pairs.

title: Combat spell training max threshold
text: Only cast the Combat spell training spells when more than this many creatures are in combat with you.

title: Combat teaching skill
text: A combat skill to teach your hunting buddies while fighting, for example Small Edged.

title: Combat trainer action count
text: How many attacks to make with a weapon before swapping to the next when the mind state goal is not reached.

title: Combat trainer focus threshold
text: Once every weapon being trained is at or above this mind state, stay on one weapon longer instead of switching often. 0 turns this off; 10 or more turns it on.

title: Combat trainer gain check
text: Main-hand attack rounds in a row with no mind state gain (locked, creature too weak, constant misses) before the weapon is swapped or set aside. 0 turns it off; 5 is a good start.

title: Combat trainer gear set
text: The gear set from the Gear Sets page put back on when the hunt returns to the safe room. Blank uses the set called standard.

title: Combat trainer herbs allowhands
text: Setting to override combat-trainer skipping herbs that require a hand to use while in combat Yes or No.

title: Combat trainer ignore weapon mindstate
text: Tells Ct to ignore mindstates, allowing one to farm whilst mindlocked, or with capped weapons Yes or No.

title: Combat trainer loop tick
text: Seconds the combat loop pauses between passes. Lower reacts faster; higher uses less of the computer. Blank is 0.1.

title: Combat trainer magic gain check
text: Casts of one magic skill in a row with no mind state gain before that skill is set aside for the hunt.

title: Combat trainer offhand gain check
text: Like the gain check above, for the off hand. 0 turns it off; 2 is a good start.

title: Combat trainer offhand trainables
text: Yes: use the Aiming trainables only in the off hand, so they do not compete with main-hand attacks. Needs the focus threshold above turned on. Yes or No.

title: Combat trainer target increment
text: How many mind states to gain with a weapon before moving to the next one.

title: Combat trainer use yiamura
text: Whether to use a yiamura in combat Yes or No.

title: Combat training abilities target
text: Mind state at which the Training abilities are skipped.

title: Custom hunting zones
text: Your own room lists for hunting zones: zone name to list of room numbers. A zone named here replaces the one in the Data Editor's Hunting zones.

title: Custom loot type
text: The word after LOOT when looting creatures: treasure, equipment or all. Blank uses the game's default.

title: Custom spell prep
text: A preparation command to use instead of PREPARE for every combat spell, for example invoke. A spell row's own customprep wins over this.

title: Cycle armors
text: List of armor types and corresponding items from gear to rotate for training purposes.

title: Cycle armors hysteresis
text: Choose Yes to keep the currently worn armor when every configured armor skill is trained. Choose No to swap back to the Default armor type. Yes or No.

title: Cycle armors regalia
text: A list of armor skills for trader regalia casting.

title: Cycle armors time
text: Seconds between checks for swapping armor when Cycle armors is set.

title: Cyclic no release
text: List of cyclic spells that won't get released by scripts when generally releasing cyclics A list.

title: Damaris weapon sets
text: For weapons that change form: a group name to the weapon's descriptions in each form. The current form is found at the start of combat.

title: Dance actions
text: Actions sent, in order, while dancing with a creature between attacks, for example [perc, hide]. A list.

title: Dance actions stealth
text: The same as Dance actions, used instead while Stealth still needs training. A list.

title: Dance skill
text: What weapon skill to use while dancing

title: Dance threshold
text: Defines the number of monsters you will keep in combat with you by performing 'dance actions' or attacking with only 'harmless: true' spells. 0 means kill everything.

title: Default armor type
text: With Cycle armors: the armor type to wear once every type on the list is trained, for example Plate Armor.

title: Default stance
text: Stance combat-trainer will go into when first starting up, before combat logic starts

title: Dirt stacker
text: Thief: the noun of the worn dirt stacker used for Ambush Choke; dirt is pushed out of it before the choke. Blank: no choke.

title: Dissect and butcher
text: Attempts to Necromancer dissect after butchering. Yes or No.

title: Dont stalk
text: Yes: never STALK while Stealth is in Training abilities; only hide. Yes or No.

title: Doublestrike trainables
text: When prioritizing doublestrike maneuvers, this is the list of melee one-handed skills that when equipped in your mainhand you want to attempt a doublestrike with another listed weapon skill equipped in your offhand, assuming they aren't the same item (e.g. ristes). This setting is necessary if you use twohanded staves or polearms so that you can opt them out of doublestrike attempts because they w

title: Dual load
text: Yes: load the bow with two arrows when the game allows it (Bow 201 or more, agility and reflex 30 or more, See the Wind, Eagle or Khri Steady up). Cannot be used together with a Bow row in Charged maneuvers. Yes or No.

title: Dump item count
text: How many junk items to collect before dumping them.

title: Dump junk
text: Yes: dump the junk made by braiding and other training actions. Yes or No.

title: Dynamic dance skill
text: Yes: pick the dance skill automatically from the weapons that are least trained. Yes or No.

title: Egg
text: Define the noun to turn on egg usage in combat. Cooldown is 15 minutes.

title: Empty hunting room messages
text: A list of possible messages to say when you enter a room and don't see anyone. Sample messages below if you want to add to your yaml. A list.

title: Fatigue regen action
text: What to do when fatigue falls below the threshold below, for example sit or meditate. Kept up until rested.

title: Fatigue regen threshold
text: Fatigue percent below which the fatigue action is taken.

title: Favor goal
text: Number of favors to shoot for.

title: Favor god
text: Your immortal for favors, for example Chadatru. With a Favor goal, the hunt rubs the stored favor orb.

title: Favor orb rub frequency
text: Seconds between rubs of the stored favor orb in combat.

title: Firing delay
text: Delay for shooting aimed weapons.

title: Flame expertise training threshold
text: Minimum EXP to maintain for use with analyze combos. Will Flame if your Expertise is below this threshold.

title: Flame inner fire threshold
text: Minimum inner fire to trigger analyze flame use

title: Forage item
text: If you choose forage method, you'll want to select a custom item for best learning rate.

title: Force unhide
text: Yes: come out of hiding after a Stealth training ability instead of staying hidden. Yes or No.

title: Have telescope
text: Yes: you carry a telescope, so the hunt can observe the sky for Astrology. Yes or No.

title: Combat logout health threshold
text: During Combat Trainer, send EXIT when vitality falls below this percentage. During Hunt, first issue AVOID ALL and EXIT to leave the hunting area. This is separate from AFK Monitor's vitality/spirit logout threshold.

title: Hide type
text: The hiding command: hide, or stalk to use slip stalk.

title: Hunting buddies
text: Friends who hunt the same zones. When you list each other, the hunt shares a room with them instead of moving on. A list.

title: Hunting buddies max
text: Max number of hunting buddies you want in room with you

title: Hunting disable room descriptions
text: Yes: turn room descriptions off while hunting and back on when the hunt ends.

title: Hunting info
text: The hunt entries this character runs, in order. Each entry is one hunt with its zone(s), how long to stay, and the skills that end it early. "Add item" on the Hunting info row creates a new entry with these fields ready to fill in. A named hunt (Hunt picker at the top) can carry its own copy of this list. A list.

title: Hunting nemesis
text: A list of nemesis or people you do not want to hunt with. A list.

title: Hunting room max searches
text: When unable to find a room to hunt in, hunting-buddy will run back to a safe room and wait 20-40 seconds before returning to the hunting zone to look for a room again. How many times should hunting-buddy revist the area to look for a suitable hunting room before ultimately giving up? Note, this is not the number of physical rooms to be checked. This is the number of times to wait then revisit the

title: Hunting room min mana
text: Minimum mana the room must show to PERCEIVE before the hunt settles there. 0 does not check.

title: Hunting room strict mana
text: Yes: never settle for a room with less mana than the minimum. No: use an empty room anyway when none has enough mana. Yes or No.

title: Ignored npcs
text: NPCs to ignore in combat, WM familiars are a common one. Without ignoring them you may appraise them. A list.

title: Import constructs list
text: Yes: treat every creature on the game's construct list as a construct, so construct-only attacks and spells are used on them.

title: Import undeads list
text: Yes: treat every creature on the game's undead list as undead, so undead-only attacks and spells are used on them.

title: Khri adaptation
text: Thief only - use khri adaptation Can use PUNCTURE, SLICE, IMPACT, FIRE, COLD, or ELECTRIC, delay type or type delay slice, slice, etc

title: Kneel khri
text: Thief only - kneel to activate khri With sufficient skill, you can activate while standing Yes or No.

title: Last rites
text: Yes: perform last rites on corpses after looting (Cleric). Yes or No.

title: Left hand free
text: Yes: keep the left hand empty while aiming the bow, so the Aiming trainables are not used. Yes or No.

title: Loot bodies
text: Yes: loot creatures after killing them. Yes or No.

title: Loot delay
text: Delay for looting bodies, in seconds

title: Loot specials
text: Special handling for particular loot: rows of name (the item) and bag (the container it goes in). A list.

title: Lootables
text: The game's list of items worth looting. Do not change it here; add to it with Loot additions.

title: Lore exp training max threshold
text: Mind state at which the Lore skills listed under Stop on count as done.

title: Magic exp training max threshold
text: Mind state at which the Magic skills listed under Stop on count as done. Blank is 32.

title: Maneuver rush engage only
text: Yes: use the shield rush maneuver only to close in on a creature, never as a training attack. Yes or No.

title: Maneuver rush shield
text: With Charged Maneuver in Training abilities or Pounce to engage: the shield to rush with, for example buckler.

title: Maneuver rush skip retreat
text: Set to true to avoid retreating if already at melee. Yes or No.

title: Maneuver rush to engage
text: Toggle use of Maneuver Rush to engage (when it is available) Yes or No.

title: Manipulate only to train
text: Yes: Empath manipulation is used only while Empathy still trains. No: always manipulate when enough creatures are present. Yes or No.

title: Manipulate threshold
text: How many creatures must be in combat with you before Empath manipulation starts.

title: Meditation pause timer
text: Used to set a pause timer for barbarian meditations. This number should go down with a chakrel, circles, and stats... When buff or combat-trainer scripts are activating meditations, this is how many seconds to wait for it to activate.

title: Necro corpse priority
text: Necromancer: with a corpse, pet first (raise a zombie or bone bug) or heal first (the healing rituals). Blank is heal.

title: Necro force rituals
text: Yes: perform the Necromancer rituals whether or not Thanatology still trains. Yes or No.

title: Necro redeemed
text: Yes: a Redeemed Necromancer; only the dissect ritual is allowed. Yes or No.

title: Necro siphon vit threshold
text: Vitality percent below which Siphon Vitality is cast, as set in Necromancer healing.

title: Necromancer healing
text: Necromancer healing: one row per spell with its wound and vitality thresholds. Works with the Thanatology settings. Consume Flesh needs the body part, which GrayDR does not read yet. A table of name and value pairs.

title: Offensive spell cycle
text: The order to cast the Offensive spells in, by name. Leave empty to take them as listed. A list.

title: Offensive spell mana threshold
text: Do not cast offensive, buff or training spells when mana is at or below this.

title: Offensive spells
text: The spells Combat Trainer casts at enemies, in order. "Add item" creates a spell entry with its fields ready to fill in. Name, skill, and mana are the ones every entry needs; the rest are optional. A list.

title: Offhand thrown
text: Yes: thrown weapons may be used in the off hand. Yes or No.

title: OST use waggle
text: The name of a buff set whose spells are cast as the offensive spells, in place of the Offensive spells list. Blank: not used.

title: Paladin use badge
text: Yes: pray with the pilgrim badge in combat whenever its cooldown allows (Paladin). Yes or No.

title: Paladin use mana glyph
text: Yes: watch for the Glyph of Mana running out and renew it (Paladin). Yes or No.

title: Permashocked
text: Yes: you are permanently shocked, so every creature is treated as a construct without naming them. Yes or No.

title: Pounce on cooldown
text: Toggle to use Pounce ability (for rangers) every time it is available Yes or No.

title: Pounce to engage
text: Toggle to use Pounce ability (for Rangers) instead of engage (when it is off cooldown) Yes or No.

title: Prep scaling factor
text: With Use auto mana: the discern limit is multiplied by this to get the mana to prepare with, for example 0.8.

title: Prioritize maneuver doublestrike
text: Yes: with Charged Maneuver in Training abilities, go for doublestrikes by briefly switching the training weapon. Yes or No.

title: Prioritize offensive spells
text: Yes: the Offensive spells are cast before the Combat spell training spells. No: training spells come first. Yes or No.

title: Priority defense
text: Set a priority defense skill name to always use 100% of that defense when it's legal for your weapon.

title: Priority weapons
text: List of weapon skills to focus training on. A list of weapon skill names.

title: Release cyclic on low mana
text: Yes: release the running cyclic spell when mana falls under the threshold below. Yes or No.

title: Release cyclic threshold
text: Mana below which the cyclic is released.

title: Retreat threshold
text: Retreat and stay out of combat when this many creatures or more are fighting you.

title: Roar helm noun
text: Set the noun of your roar helm to use scream helm before roars.

title: Safety concentration minimum
text: Concentration below which the hunt backs off to recover. Blank: not checked.

title: Safety escape health threshold
text: Health percent below which the hunt escapes the room. Blank is 80.

title: Stop hunting below vitality
text: Vitality percent. When your vitality falls under this number the hunt leaves at once, retreats before anything else, skips the last kill, puts weapons away, runs the hunt row's after scripts and walks to the safe room. Master Train sees it as the hunt result Low vitality. While a hunt with this set is running, the AFK Monitor leaves low vitality to the hunt instead of logging out. 0 turns it off.

title: Segue prep on stop
text: Bard: the preparation word used for the segue spell below, for example prepare.

title: Segue spell on stop
text: Bard: a cyclic spell to segue into instead of releasing the running cyclic when the hunt ends. Must be a spell you know.

title: Sell loot skip bank
text: Yes: the Sell Loot run after a hunt skips the bank. Yes or No.

title: Skip last kill
text: When combat-trainer is ending, kill the last mob or not, you will potentially lose ammo if you don't Yes or No.

title: Sliver recast delay
text: Moon Mage: seconds between casts of the Starlight Sphere slivers. Blank is 180.

title: Stance override
text: Override automatic handling of your stances during combat.

title: Stances
text: Your stance per weapon skill, named as in Weapon training: evasion, parry and shield numbers, or a saved stance name. A table of name and value pairs.

title: Stealth attack aimed action
text: A special ranged attack to use from hiding, for example snipe or poach.

title: Stomp to engage
text: Toggle to use War Stomp instead of engage (when it is available) Yes or No.

title: Stop hunting if bleeding
text: Yes: stop the hunt the moment you start bleeding, so you can be healed before you bleed out. No tending in combat. Yes or No.

title: Stop on familiar drag
text: When true, will stop the hunt when a familiar drags you from combat when stunned. False means it will return you to the room drug from Yes or No.

title: Stop on high threshold
text: Mind state the skills under Stop on (skills at mindlock) must reach before the hunt ends. Blank is 34.

title: Stop on low threshold
text: Mind state at or below which a skill under Stop on low (skills) ends the hunt.

title: Stop to burgle
text: Yes: end the hunt early when the Burgle cooldown is ready. A named hunt can also set this on its own. Yes or No.

title: Strict weapon stance
text: When true then weapon stances are strictly respected as listed in your yaml or base.yaml settings. title: automap
text: .automap. Records the moves you make by hand so the Data Editor can put them on the travel map, dark rooms included. Nothing is sent to the game. - .automap starts recording from the room you are in. - .automap status says how many moves are recorded so far, how many were through the dark, and how many commands are waiting since the last room. - .automap stop ends it and says what was recorded. How to walk an area. Have a way to make light, but keep it off. Walk one exit at a time. In a lit room the recorder notes the move you sent, the room you arrived in, its name and its exits. When a move answers with darkness, you are in a dark room. Light up however you do it (a lantern, a gaethzen orb, a spell), then type look (or just l). The look is what shows the room, and that is the moment the recorder writes it down: its number, its name, its exits, and a mark that it is a dark room. Put the light out, then take the next exit. Do not walk around lit: a lit room never answers with darkness, so the recorder would write it down as an ordinary room. Each move becomes one row on the Data Editor's Map tab, under Walks. A row holds every command you typed between the two rooms, so for a dark room it holds the move, the light command and the look. See Data Editor, Walks.

title: Barbarian Magic
text: .barb-magic .Barb_Magic. Activate an ordered list of Barbarian abilities for training.

title: buffs
text: .buffs. Casts a named buff set once. .buffs casts the set called default, .buffs hunt casts the set called hunt. Add force to recast everything even if it is active, strict to keep going until every buff sticks, list to show this character's sets, or set=name to list the spells in one set. The sets come from the Buff configuration on the Magic page. Master Train uses the same activity for pre-hunt buffing.

title: burgle
text: .burgle. Burgles a home: enters by lockpick or rope, searches the rooms, keeps or sells the loot, as set on the Studio's Burgle page. Started by hand it keeps Lich Burgle's safety word so a typo cannot start a caper; from a Master Train card no word is needed.

title: Carving
text: .carve. Native port of carve.lic. chapter recipe material type noun, or resume type noun

title: carve-bead
text: .carve-bead. Carves a prayer bead for the Theurgy page's aspect. Words: debug, primer (use the carving primer), or an aspect name.

title: Chain
text: .chain. Run scripts and game commands one after another, separated by a pipe. Separate steps with |. Lead with a count like 3x to repeat the whole chain. Quotes work as usual.

title: collect
text: .collect. Walks to the collecting room and collects rocks until both Outdoorsmanship and Perception are done learning: mind locked, or at their rank cap.

title: Combat Trainer
text: .combat-trainer. The combat engine on its own, in the room you are standing in: it fights what is here with the weapons, armor, spells and abilities from the Combat page, without walking anywhere. Hunt is the same engine with the walking and the zone added. Words: debug, construct, undead, innocence, d20 (a dance threshold), r20 (a retreat threshold).

title: configprobe
text: .configprobe. Prints the configuration values the combat scripts depend on, for pasting into a bug report. Reads only; nothing is sent to the game.

title: Craft Training
text: .craft. Native rank-tier training port of craft.lic; knitting delegates to Sew. forging|outfitting|engineering|alchemy|enchanting [debug]

title: crystal-arcana
text: .crystal-arcana. Gazes into the worn sanowret crystal once, for Arcana.

title: Deed Sorting (Hollow Eve)
text: .deed-sort. Hand sack deeds to their keepers, then rebuild each keeper's register into full-size deeds. nothing for the party, or tidy.

title: Enchanting
text: .enchant. Native port of enchant.lic with sigil/fount/imbue handling. chapter recipe noun [base noun], or resume noun

title: engine-text-wait-report
text: .engine-text-wait-report. A test script: sends LOOK and reports the room's exits. Not for play.

title: favor
text: .favor. Gets a favor: the temple puzzle for one orb, then the altar. .favor Immortal names the immortal; otherwise the Theurgy page's aspect is used. Buys a primer when it needs one.

title: First Aid
text: .first-aid. Train First Aid and Scholarship from anatomy charts. Leave blank for First Aid, or choose Scholarship or Both.

title: Forging
text: .forge. Blacksmithing, armorsmithing, and weaponsmithing crafting, tempering, and enhancements, exactly like forge.lic and smith.lic. Book type + chapter + recipe + metal + noun, or an enhancement + noun; finish word optional.

title: go2
text: .go2. Walks you to a room. Type a room number, a map tag, or words from the room name: - go2 10028 walks to that room number (the numbers GrayDR shows, never Lich map numbers). - go2 bank walks to the nearest room tagged bank. A plural like thieves is tried as thief too. - go2 town green searches the room names. One match walks at once; several matches are listed nearest first and you type the number of the one you want. It says what it matched every time, so a wrong pick leaves a trace. It works without the dot because it is listed under Bare commands on the Commands page. While walking, a way that is closed to this character (a gate that refuses, a crossing that is not there) is marked and another route is tried; it stops when no other route exists. .k stops a walk.

title: handoff-receive
text: .handoff-receive. The receiver's side of a handoff when his Master Train is not running. It is started on his window by the giver's script; you do not start it yourself.

title: handofftest
text: .handofftest. A real handoff with the receiver, on demand, from an idle giver: full pouches from the configured container, the scroll chest, and the boxes, exactly as Master Train's own handoff does it. .handofftest pouches, scrolls or boxes limits it to those kinds; no word means all three. A receiver running Master Train does his side at his next safe moment; an idle receiver gets his receiver script started for him.

title: haul-to-2014100
text: .haul-to-2014100. A test walk to the Crossing south ferry dock by way of the ferry. Not for play; use go2.

title: haul-to-241002
text: .haul-to-241002. A test walk to the Crossing south ferry dock by way of the ferry. Not for play; use go2.

title: Healme
text: .healme. Heals the configured Empath's wounds, scars, vitality, poison and disease. A number sets the severity to heal from; debug prints each decision.

title: hospital-heal
text: .hospital-heal. Heals at the Empath's plant room when one is configured on the Healing page, otherwise at Quentin's hospital. .hospital-heal force runs the whole visit even with no injuries found.

title: Hunt
text: .hunt. Hunts: walks to the hunting zone, finds a room with creatures, and runs the combat engine there with the weapons, armor, spells and abilities from the Combat page. It leaves for the reasons set on that page: a skill threshold reached, low vitality, bleeding, the time limit, the encumbrance limit, the boxes limit, a familiar drag, Burgle becoming ready, or a manual stop. In Master Train each reason can start its own activities (Hunt Results). .hunt runs the main hunt, the character's own settings. A named hunt, with its own values on the Combat page, is run from a Master Train Hunt card that names it.

title: Inventory Spreadsheet
text: .inventory-spreadsheet. Records the carried, eddy and vault items and writes a CSV for Google Sheets. Words: status, resume (continue a vault restore), stop-cleanup, help.

title: kiosk
text: .kiosk. The Trader kiosk. .kiosk makes sure the kiosk is up in the kiosk room (summons or refreshes it) with the markup set; .kiosk maintain refreshes it when it is close to expiring; .kiosk service takes everything it holds, tops the reserve up from the bank and sells the crystalline bundles at the furrier; .kiosk status prints CONC and STUDY and changes nothing. Settings are on the Trading Training page under Trader kiosk. The tessera leaves its container only for the cast and for POKE, TAP and TOUCH, and goes straight back.

title: lichroom
text: .lichroom. Translates between GrayDR room numbers and Lich map numbers. .lichroom for this room, .lichroom 2026011 for that room, .lichroom lich 8908 the other way.

title: Locksmithing
text: .locksmithing. Train Locksmithing with daily and consumable training boxes. Use once to perform one trainer pick for combat-training integration.

title: Make Steel
text: .makesteel. Buy iron and coal, smelt steel ingots, optionally refine them, exactly like makesteel.lic. Number of ingots (1-21), then optionally l, m, or h for carbon content (default h), then optionally refine.

title: master-train
text: .master-train. Runs your whole training routine, card by card, as set up on the Studio's Master Train page. Every command it takes is in Typed commands.

title: Medic Check
text: .medic-check .medic_check. Heal configured patients, maintain the bonded plant, and recover in the healing room.

title: Medic Plant
text: .medic-plant. Maintains and fully drains the Empath's bonded vela'tohr plant in the medic room. Words, all optional: room=number, set=name, healing-set=name, recovery-set=name, recast=n, max-score=n, resume-score=n, foc-score=n, min-vitality=n, keep-regen, once, debug.

title: Memory Orbs
text: .memory-orbs .orbs. Invokes or studies memory orbs and puts the orbs that were not used back in their container. An orb that cannot be used goes to the trash bin room from the Character page.

title: Mix calculator
text: .mixcalc. Volumes of pure metal and magic ingot for a 67/33 mix of a given size. First number is the volume you need. Second number, optional, is the volume of 67/33 you already have.

title: Moon Mage Perceive
text: .moon-perc. One Attunement pass over the Moon Mage perceive targets; skipped when Attunement is mind locked.

title: Multi
text: .multi. Repeat an ordered mixture of game commands and child scripts. Put the repeat count first or last. Prefix child scripts with a colon or semicolon; separate entries with commas, or use semicolons when no commas are present.

title: om
text: .om. Creates and loads an Osrel Meraud from one exact deity favor orb. It never uses a bare get my orb, which could pick up an unrelated memory orb.

title: Performance
text: .performance. Train Performance with the configured instrument. Choose a mindstate goal from 1 to 34. noclean and checksong are also available.

title: Lockbox Picking
text: .pick. Disarms and picks the boxes from the configured box sources, walking to the picking room first when one is set. Words: refill (only refill the lockpicks), all (ignore mind lock), stand, quick, normal, careful or blind (the assumed difficulty), source=container, debug.

title: plat
text: .plat. Money converter. .plat 30 dokoras shows that amount in copper and what it is worth in Kronars and Lirums. The currency word can be shortened to its first three letters. Sends nothing to the game.

title: pouch-appraisal
text: .pouch-appraisal. Appraises the training gem pouches from the pouch source container and moves each finished one to the staging container, as set on the Gem Pouches page. With no pouch adjective configured it does nothing.

title: Profit Tracker
text: .profit-tracker. Reports what hunting, crafting and burgling have earned. The recording itself runs in the background while the tracker is enabled on the Profit Tracker page.

title: profit-tracker-service
text: .profit-tracker-service. The background half of the Profit Tracker. Started by GrayDR when the tracker is enabled on the Profit Tracker page; you do not start it yourself.

title: Reconnect Recovery
text: .reconnect-recovery. Put a reconnected character back in order before Master Train resumes. No arguments.

title: Remedies
text: .remedy. Native port of remedy.lic. remedies chapter recipe herb1 herb2 catalyst container noun, or continue ...

title: repair-dropoff
text: .repair-dropoff. Drops worn armour and shield with the repairer by REPAIR ALL, hands over every other gear item that is not marked never for repair, and stows every ticket. It does not wait for the repairs. Money: starts with 100 platinum, tops up 20 when the repairer needs more, finishes at the bank with 20 platinum.

title: repair-pickup
text: .repair-pickup. Gives every repair ticket back, waits when a repair is not ready, stores returned gear (tied for belt tools, stowed otherwise), and wears everything from the worn-gear sack, which must report empty before it is thrown in the repairer's bucket. It never leaves the repairer's room. A sack that cannot be proven empty stops it with the sack in hand.

title: Rezz
text: .rezz. Cleric resurrection of a dead player in the room (rezz [player]).

title: Safe Room Healing
text: .safe-room. Select configured PC Empath, self-healing, NPC, or Necromancer healing routes. Use skip to remain in the current room or force to run healing logic without visible wounds.

title: Scholarship Training
text: .scholarship-train. Studies a tailoring book page by page, a Tome of Lore first, with a song playing alongside until Performance is mind locked.

title: Scroll Manage
text: .scroll-manage. Sort loose spell scrolls from the backpack and the chest in the backpack into the two eternity scroll folios, exactly like the custom scroll-manage Lich script. Runs after a handoff hands Tirax scrolls. No arguments. The word help shows the usage.

title: Sell Loot
text: .sell-loot. Sell configured loot and perform optional banking.

title: Tailoring
text: .sew. Sew, knit, or enhance tailoring items exactly like sew.lic, including consumable restocking and rental renewal. hold|log|stow|trash + type/chapter/recipe/material/noun, or instructions form, seal/reinforce/lighten, or resume <noun>.

title: Shaping
text: .shape. Shape wood items exactly like shape.lic, including consumable restocking by chapter, assembly parts, and bow enhancements. hold|log|stow|trash + chapter/recipe/material/noun [skip], or instructions form, laminate/lighten/cable <noun>, or resume <noun>.

title: Smelt
text: .smelt. Work a loaded crucible until the metal is mixed, exactly like smelt.lic. Leave blank to smelt a crucible you loaded yourself. Type refine to pour flux over an ingot already in the crucible. Type help for the full procedure.

title: smith
text: .smith. The forging path work orders use per item: finds the recipe by name, buys the parts and optionally the ingot, walks to an anvil or the private forge (renewing the rental when it runs low), restocks oil, casts the smith buff set, then forges, with optional stamp and enhancement passes and scrap disposal. Takes the material and the item name.

title: sorcery-train
text: .sorcery-train. Trains Sorcery with the Sorcery entry under Training spells on the Magic page, the same way utility-train, ward-train and aug-train train their skills. Stops at mind lock.

title: Spin Thread
text: .spin. Buy fibers and spin them into thread at a town tailoring society. Choose a material. Add fine, thin, average, thick, heavy, or yarn after it to change the wheel setting; heavy is the default.

title: Summoning Training
text: .summoning. Train Warrior Mage Summoning by summoning and breaking weapons, then focusing the pathway.

title: Tarantula
text: .tarantula. Consume eligible field experience with a biomechanical tarantula or harvester spider.

title: tendme
text: .tendme. Tends your own wounds: only parasites, lodged objects and bleeders that are safe to tend, most severe first. .tendme train unwraps and rebinds wounds for learning; .tendme monitor keeps running to keep bleeders tended.

title: tendother
text: .tendother. Binds another character's wounds and keeps the bandages up for their run: .tendother Name.

title: Theurgy
text: .theurgy. Train Theurgy using configured rituals

title: Tinkering
text: .tinker. Native port of tinker.lic including mechanisms and bow enhancements. chapter recipe material noun; resume/instructions/enhancement/mechanisms forms

title: tithe
text: .tithe. Puts the tithe in the almsbox, as set on the Theurgy page. Theurgy training calls it by itself; run it alone to tithe now.

title: trader-perc
text: .trader-perc. One Attunement pass over the Trader perceive targets (mana, planets, illusion). Does nothing when Attunement is already mind locked.

title: Trading Training
text: .trading-train. Sells the profit pouches and runs Mags's nuloe-stem task loop. Services the Trader kiosk first when one is configured.

title: Utility Magic Training
text: .utility-train. Train Utility magic using the script-owned spell configuration.

title: validate
text: .validate. Checks this character's whole configuration against the data files (skill names, spells, the map, activities, the gear list, hunting zones, crafting tools) and prints every value that cannot be right. Reads only; nothing is sent to the game.

title: Wait
text: .wait. Pause a script sequence for a number of seconds. Enter the number of seconds to pause. This is commonly used inside Multi as :wait N.

title: Walking Astrology
text: .walkingastro. Train Astrology in the background while hunting or crafting - observe through the telescope whenever the sky is visible and predict when a pool fills, exactly like walkingastro.lic. Runs until stopped. Optional "debug" prints the toggle states and each decision.

title: Warding Magic Training
text: .ward-train. Train Warding magic using the script-owned spell configuration.

title: weargear
text: .weargear. Puts a gear set back on from wherever the pieces are. .weargear re-wears the standard set, .weargear name another set from the Gear Sets page. It exists for the day a script dies between stripping your armour and putting it back.

title: Weave Cloth
text: .weave-cloth. Weave two thread items into cloth at a town tailoring society.

title: Work Orders
text: .workorders. Request, craft, bundle, and turn in crafting-society work orders, exactly like workorders.lic. Discipline plus optional repair, turnin, or continue (resume the order the logbook is already tracking).

title: wrayth-prime
text: .wrayth-prime. Sends the client controls that unlock the game's larger typeahead queue, then exits. No game commands. Runs by itself at login while Prime client controls at login is on (Character page).

title: Yiamura
text: .yiamura. Operates a worn yiamura: .yiamura raise, point, observe, invoke or reset. The hunt raises it by itself; the knowledge it gathers is collected by Yiamura Claim.

title: Yiamura Claim
text: .yiamura-claim. Collect the knowledge the yiamura's observer gathered during a hunt (OBSERVE MY YIAMURA). Does nothing when there is nothing to claim.

title: Zasele Tasks (Hollow Eve)
text: .zasele. Seamstress Zasele's sewing and knitting tasks on Andreshlew, turned in for woven sacks. Nothing for the loop. "repair" drops the outfitting tools at Catrox (the loop collects the tickets).

title: GrayDR manual
text: GrayDR is a DragonRealms front end with its own script engine built in. It replaces Lich: the scripts run inside GrayDR, every setting lives in the Configuration Studio, and the game data the scripts rely on is edited in the Data Editor.  This manual is rebuilt every time a new GrayDR package is made, so the settings tables always match the GrayDR you are running.

title: The map picture
text: Type .map to open the community map picture for the area you are in. You are drawn on it when the map knows your room, and clicking a room on the picture walks you there.

Open it with Launch Data Editor.  Scripts read these files the next time they start. Nothing is written until you press SAVE CHANGES (Ctrl+S); a changed tab is marked with a star. For each spell: the guild, the skill it trains, the abbreviation PREPARE takes, the default mana, the mana type, whether it is prepared or targeted, when a buff is recast, and the game lines:  - Lines that mean the cast worked: the line the game prints when the spel

title: Hunting zones
text: Each zone is a name and a list of room numbers, in the order the hunt tries them. Use the zone name in a character's hunting settings exactly as written. A zone name may hold letters, digits, and - only.

text: For every game command a script sends: the lines that mean it worked, the lines that mean the game refused, the lines that ask for it to be sent again to confirm, and whether silence is a real answer. A command whose answer is not here stops the script that sent it. Paste the game line; for several, one per row.

text: For the Hollow Eve Zasele tasks: the materials to keep, who holds each material family, and the deed words asked for.

text: For each craft, the tools it needs and the tools used only if the character owns them. The Notes list is for your own reference.

title: Map
text: The Map tab fixes travel without anyone's help. Use the Show box to pick a section.

The Requires row names what the move needs, in one of two shapes: Athletics at least 100 (a skill and the rank), or Citizenship is Zoluren (a fact that must match). Each row is one move: the room you left, every command you sent between the two rooms, the room you arrived in with its name and exits, and how many times the game answered darkness on the way. text: Saves everything, then rebuilds the travel map and puts it into every GrayDR package. GrayDR must be closed first; Apply refuses while a game window or Engine Host is running. It takes a minute or two and writes a report, map-report.txt, in the package folder, saying what went in and what was refused.

text: 1. Have a way to make light, but keep it off. Type .automap in the game window. 2. Walk the area by hand, one exit at a time, every exit you want on the map. 3. When a move answers with darkness, you are in a dark room: light up (lantern, gaethzen orb, spell, whatever you use), type l (or look), and the room shows and is recorded with its number, exits and the dark mark. Beside the packages sits one set of launchers that always point at the newest package, so you never have to find the right folder yourself:  Launcher Opens Launch GrayDR The game window. GrayDR keeps the login itself; you do not type the password again. - Each row is one character. Launch logs that character in. Tick several rows and press Launch All to log them in one after another, top to bottom; the

title: Profiles
text: A profile is one complete set of settings. The Profile menu creates and loads them. Most people have one, called default. The Configuration Studio always edits the profile that is loaded.

title: When something changes
text: - A change you save in the Configuration Studio is read by the next script that starts. You do not restart GrayDR for it. - A new package needs GrayDR closed and started again from the launcher. - A change in the Data Editor is read the next time a script starts.

title: Scripts
text: Every script, grouped the way the Configuration Studio groups their settings. Start a script by typing its name after a dot in the game window, for example .workorders tailoring. Typed commands covers starting, stopping and listing scripts.

title: AFK Monitor
text: Script name: afk  Watch an idle character; answer idle warnings, dodge justice, escape traps, and log out on death or low vitality. It never sends beside another script - when it must act it stops the other scripts first, then acts alone.

title: How to start it
text: Type .afk in the game window.  In Master Train, pick AFK Monitor as the activity and put the same words in its Arguments box.

title: Configuration Studio
text: Every setting GrayDR and its scripts use lives here. Open it from the Settings menu of a game window, or with Launch Configuration Studio when no window is open. One page per settings page lists every field.

title: How it is laid out
text: The left-hand list has two groups.  - GLOBAL SETTINGS: one value for every character. The Commands page and the Memory diagnostics page are here, and so is the global copy of every setting that can be set either way. - CHARACTER SETTINGS: values for the character chosen in the Character box at the top. Two pages here are built differently: Gear and Master Train.  A setting that can be set either w

title: Hunts
text: The Hunt box beside the character picks which settings you are editing:  - Main hunt (character settings): the character's own values. - A named hunt: its own layer on top of the character's values. Anything you do not change in the hunt comes from the character.  Add hunt... makes a named hunt. It starts as a copy of the main hunt's combat settings as they are now and is on its own from then on.

title: Guild
text: The Guild box appears when GrayDR has not yet seen this character's guild in play. Set it once; guild-specific pages and fields are shown only for characters of that guild.

title: Saving
text: Nothing is written until you press Save Changes. Save runs a Configuration check first: a value that cannot be right (a room that is not on the map, a spell the Data Editor does not know, a required field left blank) is listed, and you choose Save anyway or go back. title: Hiding and ordering fields
text: Every field has a Hide button: hide it on this page for every character, or only for this one. Organize fields... at the top of each page brings hidden fields back and lets you reorder the fields you have set. Required fields cannot be hidden.

title: The Gear page
text: Everything the character owns that scripts pick up, wear, swap, or send for repair, in one place. Scripts never guess gear; if it is not on this page, they do not know it exists.  Categories: Weapons, Armor, Shields, Brawling (no-damage items; parry devices are the exception), Other, and Crafting tools.
